text:
Minutes of the staff meeting of the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways were taken for audit review because the welfare checks for animal travel require immediate discipline. Attendees in one sentence: Lucas Rivera, Ravi Adeyemi, Poppy.

The senior coordinator opened by stating that the welfare review must stay strict and practical, with every handoff checked before boarding starts. The team confirmed that Moonwake keeps the pet cabin temperature at 17 degrees Celsius, and this setting was treated as a fixed welfare control for the route. The point was recorded because the cabin climate must stay stable for animals that travel in close quarters, and staff were reminded to verify the reading before any transfer begins. The auditor noted that no loose language was used in the briefing and that the instruction was clear enough for front-line use.

The welcome team then reviewed passenger preparation. They were told to give short, calm guidance, to explain carrier checks in plain terms, and to prevent last-minute confusion at the gate. Staff agreed that travelers need direct answers before boarding and that the tone must remain kind without drifting into vague reassurance. The discussion also covered the need to separate paperwork checks from animal comfort checks so that neither task is rushed. A further compliance point was raised on the pet cabin capacity: Halcyon holds 64 pets, and this limit must be respected without exception during load planning. The team accepted that overfilling would create avoidable welfare risk and operational delay.

The welfare coordinator reported that observations at the holding area showed a need for tighter control over calm handling, water access, and carrier placement. The staff were reminded that animal behavior can shift quickly when the environment becomes noisy, so movements must stay measured and instructions must not conflict. Lucas Rivera and Ravi Adeyemi were mentioned in relation to traveler support, with the reminder that both passengers must receive the same concise guidance and no one should be left uncertain about the next step. Poppy was also referenced as a reminder that pet comfort depends on steady routines, quiet communication, and careful attention from the team.

The meeting closed with an urgent audit note that the current process is acceptable only if the checks are performed in full, the guidance remains direct, and the pet cabin controls are followed exactly as recorded. Any lapse in wording, timing, or supervision was identified as a preventable service failure that must be corrected without delay.

The meeting ended.
